title: Band 6 vs Band 8: apa bedanya
title_target: Model answers compared and common errors
goal: Melihat dua esai untuk soal yang persis sama — satu Band 6, satu Band 8 — lalu mengenali dan memperbaiki dua belas kesalahan yang paling sering menahan penutur bahasa Indonesia di Band 6.
bekal: menunjuk penyebab pasti kenapa sebuah paragraf hanya bernilai Band 6
memperbaiki artikel, bentuk jamak, dan kesesuaian subjek-kata kerja saat memeriksa ulang
mengganti sepuluh kata Band 6 dengan alternatif Band 7+ yang kolokasinya benar

blocks.text: Cara tercepat memahami band descriptor bukan membacanya, melainkan membandingkan dua jawaban untuk soal yang sama. Kedua esai di bawah menjawab soal ini, ditulis dalam waktu yang sama, oleh dua orang dengan kosakata yang tidak terlalu jauh berbeda. Yang membedakan bukan jumlah kata sulit.
*In many large cities, traffic congestion is becoming worse every year. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?*

blocks.title: Model Band 6.0 — 265 kata
items: In nowadays, traffic jam is a big problem in many big cities in the world. This essay will discuss about the causes of this problem and also the solution.

Firstly, the main cause of traffic jam is because the number of car is increasing every year. Many people want to buy car because they have more money than before. Secondly, another cause is public transport. In many countries, public transport is not good, so people don't want to use it. Moreover, many people live in suburb and they must go to city centre every day for work, so the road become very crowded in the morning and also in the evening.

Moreover, the government must make a research about this problem. Firstly, the government should build more road and more flyover, so the car can move faster and the problem will be reduce. Secondly, the government should improve the public transport, for example bus and train. If the public transport is good, cheap and comfortable, many people will use it and they will leave their car at home. In addition, the government can make a policy like odd-even, so not all car can enter the city centre every day. This solution is already applied in many countries and it is quite successful.

In conclusion, traffic jam is caused by many car, bad public transport and also people who live far from their office. The government should build more road, improve public transport and make a good policy. If all people work together, this big problem will be solved and our city will be more comfortable.

blocks.title: Model Band 8.0 — 299 kata
items: Congestion in large cities has worsened steadily over the past two decades, and the reasons have as much to do with how cities are built as with how many cars they contain. In my view the problem has two main causes, and the measures most likely to work are those that reduce demand rather than add capacity.

The first cause is the spread of low-density housing far from workplaces. As land near the centre became unaffordable, families moved to suburbs designed around the car, so a journey that would once have been a short walk now requires a twenty-kilometre drive. Greater Jakarta illustrates the pattern: the built-up area has expanded outwards far faster than its rail network. The second cause is that driving remains artificially cheap. Fuel is subsidised in several countries, parking in city centres is often free or nominally priced, and no driver pays for the delay he imposes on everyone behind him.

Building extra lanes is the obvious response and the least effective one, because new capacity is absorbed within a few years by drivers who previously avoided the route or travelled at another time. Charging for road space directly is far more promising. Singapore's electronic road pricing, which varies by location and time of day, cut peak-hour traffic by roughly fifteen per cent and now funds the very system it competes with. Pricing works, however, only where an alternative exists, so it has to arrive with frequent buses, reliable trains and cycle routes that parents will let their children use.

In conclusion, congestion grows out of cities that separate homes from jobs and out of prices that hide the real cost of driving. Charging for road space and spending the proceeds on public transport addresses both, whereas widening roads merely postpones the day of reckoning.

blocks.text: Esai Band 6 itu **tidak kacau**. Strukturnya ada, pembacanya paham maksudnya, dan tidak ada kalimat yang tidak bisa dimengerti. Justru itu masalahnya: siswa yang menulis seperti ini merasa sudah benar dan bingung kenapa nilainya tidak naik-naik. Tabel berikut menunjukkan kenapa.

head: Kriteria
Yang dilakukan Band 6
Yang dilakukan Band 8
rows: Task Response — kedalaman ide
Sebab disebut lalu ditinggal: *another cause is public transport. In many countries, public transport is not good.* Tidak ada penjelasan kenapa, di mana, atau akibatnya.

Sebab dijelaskan sampai mekanismenya: *As land near the centre became unaffordable, families moved to suburbs designed around the car, so a journey that would once have been a short walk now requires a twenty-kilometre drive.*
Task Response — contoh
*This solution is already applied in many countries and it is quite successful.* Tidak menyebut negara, angka, atau tahun — pemeriksa tidak bisa membedakannya dari tebakan.
*Singapore's electronic road pricing … cut peak-hour traffic by roughly fifteen per cent.* Nama skema, mekanisme, dan angka: bisa diperiksa, jadi dihitung sebagai pengembangan.
Task Response — sikap
Solusi didaftar tanpa dinilai; semuanya seolah sama baiknya.

Solusi dinilai: *Building extra lanes is the obvious response and the least effective one, because new capacity is absorbed within a few years.* Menolak satu solusi dengan alasan adalah tanda berpikir, bukan menghafal.
Coherence & Cohesion

*Firstly · Secondly · Moreover · Firstly · Secondly · In addition* — penghubung dipasang di depan kalimat seperti label, bahkan *Moreover* dipakai untuk membuka paragraf solusi yang seharusnya kontras. Paragraf dua memuat sebab DAN sudah menyerempet solusi.

Penghubung eksplisit sedikit (*however, whereas, In conclusion*); sisanya kohesi lewat rujukan: *The first cause … The second cause … Pricing works, however, only where …* Satu paragraf, satu pekerjaan.
Lexical Resource
*problem* 6 kali, *traffic jam* 4 kali, *good* 3 kali, *the government should* 3 kali. *Make a research*, *make a policy*, *make a big problem* — satu kata kerja untuk segalanya.
*congestion, worsened, low-density housing, unaffordable, absorbed, artificially cheap, nominally priced, peak-hour traffic, the proceeds, postpones*. Kolokasi tepat dan tidak ada yang dipaksakan.
Grammatical Range & Accuracy

Kesalahan dasar berulang: *in nowadays, the number of car, buy car, live in suburb, the road become, more road, many car, will be reduce, discuss about*. Hampir semua kalimat berpola subjek-verba-objek pendek.

Kalimat kompleks yang terkendali: *a journey that would once have been a short walk now requires …*, *drivers who previously avoided the route*, *cycle routes that parents are willing to let their children use*. Tidak ada kesalahan yang mengganggu.

blocks.text: Kesimpulan yang penting: jarak Band 6 ke Band 8 hampir seluruhnya soal **kedalaman ide, kesalahan kecil yang berulang, dan penghubung yang dipasang seperti label**. Tidak ada satu pun kata langka di esai Band 8 yang tidak kamu kenal.

sections.title: Dua belas kesalahan yang paling mahal

blocks.text: Semua ini muncul di esai Band 6 di atas, dan semuanya khas penutur bahasa Indonesia — bukan karena kosakatanya kurang, tapi karena bahasa Indonesia tidak menandai artikel, jamak, dan kesesuaian subjek-kata kerja, jadi telingamu tidak protes.

head: Salah
Benar
Kenapa
rows: *In nowadays, traffic is getting worse.*
*Nowadays, traffic is getting worse.* · lebih baik: *Traffic has been getting worse over the past decade.*
*Nowadays* sudah berarti *at the present time*; tidak pernah didahului preposisi. Frasa yang lebih aman: sebutkan periodenya.
*The number of car is increasing.*
*The number of cars is increasing.*
*The number of* selalu diikuti kata benda **jamak**, tapi kata kerjanya **tunggal** karena subjeknya *the number*.
*Many people want to buy car.*
*Many people want to buy a car.*
Kata benda tunggal yang bisa dihitung tidak pernah berdiri tanpa artikel. Ini kesalahan nomor satu penutur Indonesia.
*The road become very crowded.*
*The roads become very crowded.* · *The road becomes very crowded.*
Subjek jamak butuh verba tanpa *-s*; subjek tunggal butuh *-s*. Pilih satu, jangan campur.
*The government must make a research.*
*The government must conduct research.* · *… do more research.*
*Research* tidak bisa dihitung: tanpa *a*, tanpa *-s*. Kolokasi bakunya *conduct / carry out / do research*, bukan *make*.
*This essay will discuss about the causes.*
*This essay will discuss the causes.* · lebih baik: hilangkan kalimatnya.
*Discuss* sudah transitif. Bandingkan *talk about* yang memang butuh *about*. Kalimat *This essay will discuss …* sendiri sebaiknya diganti thesis statement.
*Government should build more road.*
*The government should build more roads.*
Dua kesalahan sekaligus: *the* hilang di depan institusi tertentu, dan *more* menuntut bentuk jamak.
*The problem will be reduce.*
*The problem will be reduced.*
Setelah *be* dalam kalimat pasif, verba memakai bentuk ketiga. *Will be reduce* terbaca sebagai kesalahan sistematis, bukan salah ketik.
*People are more prefer to drive.*
*People prefer to drive.* · *People are more likely to drive.*
*Prefer* adalah kata kerja penuh, tidak perlu *be* dan tidak punya bentuk *more*.
*Since long time ago, cars are increasing.*
*Car numbers have risen steadily since the 1990s.*
Kejadian yang mulai di masa lalu dan berlanjut sampai sekarang memakai *present perfect*, bukan *present continuous*.
*Many countries have same problem.*
*Many countries face the same problem.*
*The* wajib di depan *same*. Dan *have a problem* kalah tepat dibanding *face · experience · struggle with a problem*.
*According to my opinion, …*
*In my view, …* · *I would argue that …*
*According to* dipakai untuk sumber lain, bukan diri sendiri. Ini juga kesempatan bagus untuk menghindari *I think* yang diulang.

blocks.title: Cara memburunya dalam tiga menit terakhir
items: **Menit 1 — kata benda.** Telusuri esaimu dan berhenti di setiap kata benda tunggal yang bisa dihitung. Ada *a*, *an*, *the*, atau kata milik di depannya? Kalau tidak, tambahkan atau jamakkan. Ini menyembuhkan kira-kira sepertiga kesalahanmu.

**Menit 2 — kata kerja.** Lihat subjek tiap kalimat, lalu verbanya. Subjek tunggal orang ketiga (*the government, a student, this policy*) wajib berakhiran *-s* di present tense. Periksa juga bentuk ketiga setelah *be* dan *have*.

**Menit 3 — dua hal terakhir.** (a) Hitung jumlah kata secara kasar: kalikan jumlah kata di satu baris penuh dengan jumlah baris. Di bawah 250, tambahkan satu kalimat contoh, bukan satu kalimat kesimpulan. (b) Baca kalimat pertama tiap paragraf berurutan — kalau rangkaiannya sudah terbaca sebagai jawaban soal, strukturmu aman.

Yang **tidak** perlu dilakukan di tiga menit terakhir: menyisipkan kata sulit. Kata yang dipilih terburu-buru hampir selalu salah kolokasinya, dan kesalahan kosakata lebih terlihat daripada kosakata sederhana.

blocks.text: Yang membuat Lexical Resource naik bukan kata langka, melainkan kata **tepat dengan kolokasi yang benar**. Tabel ini berisi kata-kata Band 6 yang paling sering diulang, beserta penggantinya lengkap dengan pasangan katanya — hafalkan frasanya, bukan kata tunggalnya.

head: Band 6
Band 7+ (dengan kolokasinya)
Contoh kalimat
rows: big problem
a serious problem · a pressing issue · a growing concern
*Congestion has become a pressing issue in every large Asian city.*
many people
a substantial proportion of · a growing number of · the majority of
*A growing number of commuters now travel more than an hour each way.*
good public transport
reliable · frequent · affordable public transport
*People abandon their cars only where trains are frequent and affordable.*
make better
improve · upgrade · strengthen
*Cities should upgrade suburban rail before charging drivers.*
stop the problem
tackle · address · curb · alleviate
*Road pricing is one of the few measures that genuinely curbs demand.*
give money
fund · subsidise · allocate funding to
*Revenue from the charge is allocated to bus services.*
bad for
detrimental to · harmful to
*Exhaust fumes are detrimental to children's lung development.*
very common
widespread · prevalent
*Car ownership is now widespread among middle-income families.*
because of
owing to · as a result of · largely attributable to
*The delays are largely attributable to poor road design.*
I think
In my view · I would argue that · It seems to me that
*I would argue that supply-side measures are self-defeating.*

blocks.title: Kata mewah yang justru menurunkan nilai
items: *Nowadays, in this modern era, since the dawn of civilisation* — pembuka hafalan. Pemeriksa mengenalinya dalam satu detik dan tidak menghitungnya sebagai kosakatamu.
*Last but not least · In a nutshell · All in all* — idiom lisan yang tidak pernah muncul di tulisan akademik. Pakai *Finally* dan *In conclusion*.
*Utilise* sebagai pengganti *use*. Di 90% kalimat, *use* lebih tepat; *utilise* hanya wajar untuk memanfaatkan sesuatu yang belum terpakai (*utilise waste heat*).
*Plethora, myriad, ubiquitous* dipakai asal-asalan. *A plethora of* berarti berlebihan sampai merugikan, bukan sekadar *banyak*; *a plethora of solutions* terbaca aneh.
*Drastically* untuk semua perubahan. *Drastic* mengandung nuansa ekstrem dan tidak menyenangkan; kenaikan kepemilikan mobil *rose sharply*, bukan *drastically increased*.
Aturan praktisnya: kalau kamu tidak pernah **membaca** kata itu dalam kalimat orang lain, jangan memakainya pertama kali di ruang ujian.

blocks.text: *An increasing number of young professionals now work from home rather than in an office. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?*

Ingat bahwa jenis soal ini meminta **timbangan**, bukan daftar. Pembukamu harus sudah mengatakan sisi mana yang lebih berat, dan kesimpulanmu harus mengatakannya lagi dengan kata lain. Model Band 7.5 ada di bagian *Pembahasan*.

items: Sebelum menulis: pilih dua keuntungan dan dua kerugian, lalu coret satu dari masing-masing sisi — sisakan yang punya contoh konkret.
Setelah menulis: jalankan checklist tiga menit di atas. Hitung berapa kata benda tunggal tanpa artikel yang kamu temukan; angka itu adalah nilai Grammatical Accuracy-mu dalam bentuk paling jujur.
Lalu bandingkan strukturmu dengan model: apakah kerugiannya benar-benar **dijawab**, atau hanya disebut lalu ditinggalkan?

exercises.prompt: Tiap kalimat memuat satu kesalahan khas. Tulis SATU kata yang benar untuk mengisi kekosongan; pilihan yang salah ditunjukkan di dalam kurung.
items: The government should ____ (make, do) more research before widening the road.
____ (In nowadays, Nowadays), most middle-income families own at least one car.
Public transport in this city ____ (are, is) still slow and unreliable.
Cycling to work has ____ (a, an) obvious advantage: it costs almost nothing.
Children spend too much time ____ (to play, playing) games on their phones.
Congestion charging would ____ (give, bring) about a genuine change in behaviour.

exercises.prompt: Pilih kalimat yang band-nya lebih tinggi.
items: (A) In nowadays, many people has a private car. (B) Car ownership has risen sharply over the past decade. ____
(A) The government should make a research about this problem. (B) The government should commission research into the causes of congestion. ____
(A) Firstly, the first cause is the number of car. Secondly, the second cause is public transport. (B) The first cause is suburban sprawl; a second, less obvious one is the low cost of driving. ____
(A) Singapore's road pricing scheme cut peak-hour traffic by roughly fifteen per cent. (B) For example, in many countries, road pricing is very successful. ____

exercises.prompt: Lengkapi dengan kata Band 7+ dari bank kata. Perhatikan kolokasinya. Pakai tiap kata paling banyak sekali.
items: Charging drivers for road space is one of the few measures that genuinely ____ demand.
Exhaust fumes from slow-moving traffic are ____ to children's lung development.
Cities should ____ a far larger share of their transport budget to cycling infrastructure.
Car ownership is now ____ among middle-income families across Southeast Asia.

exercises.prompt: TRUE kalau pernyataan tentang esai Band 8.0 di unit ini benar, FALSE kalau tidak.
items: The Band 8 essay argues that building extra lanes is the least effective response. ____
The Band 8 essay opens with the phrase *In nowadays*. ____
The Band 8 essay names a specific pricing scheme and the size of its effect. ____
The Band 8 essay begins each paragraph with *Firstly*, *Secondly* and *Moreover*. ____

answers: do — Nowadays — is — an — playing — bring

head: No
Jawaban
Kalimat sumber & alasan
rows: do
*Research* tidak bisa dihitung dan tidak berkolokasi dengan *make*. Yang baku: *do · conduct · carry out research*.
Nowadays
*Nowadays* adalah adverbia waktu yang sudah lengkap; *in nowadays* tidak ada dalam bahasa Inggris.
is
Subjeknya *public transport* — tunggal dan tak terhitung. Kata *transport* sering dikira jamak karena maknanya banyak kendaraan.
an
*Obvious* diawali bunyi vokal, jadi artikelnya *an*. Yang menentukan bunyinya, bukan hurufnya — bandingkan *a university*, *an hour*.
playing
*Spend time* selalu diikuti verba *-ing*: *spend time doing something*. Pola *spend money on something* memakai kata benda.
bring
Kolokasinya *bring about change*. *Give about* tidak ada; kalau ingin memakai *give*, kalimatnya harus *give rise to*.
B
A memuat *in nowadays* dan *many people has*. B memakai *present perfect* untuk tren yang berlanjut, plus *risen sharply* yang kolokasinya tepat.
B
*Commission research into* — kata kerja tepat, preposisi tepat, dan *research* tanpa artikel. A salah di ketiganya.
B
A memberi label tanpa isi dan mengulang *the first · the second* dua kali. B menandai urutan sambil menilai (*a second, less obvious one*) — itulah kohesi yang tidak mekanis.
A
A menyebut skema, tempat, dan besarnya efek. B memakai *for example* lalu tidak memberi contoh apa pun; *in many countries* adalah penanda Band 6 yang paling mudah dikenali pemeriksa.
curb
*Curb demand · curb spending · curb emissions* — menahan sesuatu yang sedang tumbuh. *Detrimental* tidak bisa jadi kata kerja.
detrimental
*Detrimental to* + kata benda. Perhatikan preposisinya: bukan *detrimental for*.
allocate
*Allocate money to something* — membagikan anggaran yang sudah ada. Kalau memakai *fund*, objeknya kegiatan, bukan bagian anggaran.
widespread

*Widespread* menerangkan sesuatu yang tersebar luas di banyak tempat. *Affordable* memang muat di kalimat itu secara tata bahasa, tapi mengubah artinya menjadi harga, bukan sebaran — inilah pengecohnya.
TRUE
*Building extra lanes is the obvious response and the least effective one, because new capacity is absorbed within a few years.*
FALSE
Esai Band 8 dibuka dengan *Congestion in large cities has worsened steadily over the past two decades*. Yang memakai *In nowadays* adalah esai Band 6.
TRUE
*Singapore's electronic road pricing … cut peak-hour traffic by roughly fifteen per cent.* Nama skema dan angka efeknya keduanya ada.
FALSE
Justru sebaliknya: paragrafnya dibuka *The first cause …*, *Building extra lanes …*, *In conclusion …*. Kata *Firstly* dan *Moreover* tidak muncul sama sekali.

blocks.text: Model jawaban tugas menulis — Band 7.5, 290 kata

blocks.title: Model Band 7.5 — 290 kata
items: Remote work, which a decade ago was a privilege granted to a handful of senior staff, is now the normal arrangement for a large share of younger office workers. Although it carries real costs for people early in their careers, I believe its advantages are the greater of the two.

The clearest benefit is the recovery of time and money that commuting consumes. A junior designer in Jakarta who previously spent three hours a day travelling between Bekasi and the central business district gains roughly fifteen working hours a week, along with the fare and the exhaustion. That time does not disappear into leisure alone; surveys by several large employers since 2021 have found that staff working from home report both longer sleep and slightly higher output. Remote hiring also widens the map: a company in Bandung can employ a developer in Makassar, and the developer need not abandon her family to take the job.

The disadvantages fall almost entirely on the least experienced. Much of what a graduate learns in a first job is absorbed sideways, by overhearing how a colleague handles an angry client, and video calls transmit almost none of that. Isolation is a genuine risk too, particularly for those living alone in small rented rooms.

These costs are real, but they respond to management rather than to geography. Companies that require two days a week in the office and assign every new employee a named mentor have largely closed the gap, whereas the savings in commuting cannot be recovered by any policy at all.

In conclusion, although remote work makes the first years of a career harder, its benefits in time, cost and access to talent outweigh drawbacks that a well-designed hybrid arrangement can substantially reduce.

head: Kriteria
Yang dilakukan model
rows: Task Response

Timbangan dinyatakan di pembuka (*its advantages are the greater of the two*), dipertahankan, lalu dinyatakan ulang. Kerugiannya tidak sekadar disebut: paragraf empat **menjawabnya** dan menjelaskan kenapa keuntungannya tetap lebih berat.
Coherence & Cohesion

Empat paragraf isi dengan satu pekerjaan masing-masing. Penghubung eksplisit hanya *Although, also, whereas, In conclusion*; sisanya rujukan balik (*That time*, *These costs*, *the least experienced*).
Lexical Resource

*a privilege granted to, recovery of time, absorbed sideways, transmit, isolation, hybrid arrangement, outweigh drawbacks*. Kata *work* memang berulang karena kata topik, tapi frasanya berganti: *remote work · working from home · remote hiring*.
Grammatical Range & Accuracy

Klausa relatif non-defining (*which a decade ago was a privilege*), klausa relatif panjang (*who previously spent three hours a day travelling*), *whereas* untuk kontras, dan struktur perbandingan *the greater of the two*. Artikel dan bentuk jamak konsisten.
Kenapa belum Band 8

Contoh survei disebut tanpa nama atau angka (*surveys by several large employers*), padahal contoh Jakarta-Bekasi di kalimat sebelumnya sudah menunjukkan model ini bisa lebih spesifik. Paragraf tiga juga lebih pendek daripada yang lain.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat
items: Jarak Band 6 ke Band 8 hampir seluruhnya terletak pada **kedalaman satu ide**, bukan jumlah ide. Esai Band 6 di unit ini menyebut tiga sebab dan tiga solusi; esai Band 8 menyebut dua sebab dan dua langkah, dan nilainya dua band lebih tinggi.

Kesalahan tata bahasa yang menahanmu bukan yang rumit, melainkan enam pola yang sama berulang-ulang: artikel hilang, jamak hilang, *-s* orang ketiga hilang, bentuk ketiga setelah *be*, *make* untuk segalanya, dan preposisi berlebih (*discuss about*). Tiga menit memeriksa keenam pola itu menaikkan Grammatical Accuracy lebih cepat daripada sebulan menambah kosakata.
Contoh spesifik adalah alat termurah untuk menaikkan Task Response. Satu nama kota, satu angka, satu tahun — dan paragraf yang tadinya terdengar seperti pendapat umum berubah menjadi argumen.
